builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B: Adapting a 2.6B Hybrid Model to Tajik Tool Calling, and What Continued Pretraining Takes Away
summary: The method replaces reliance on the base model's native tool-calling ability for Tajik with a two-stage recipe: LoRA continued pretraining on 1.49M Tajik documents followed by SFT on a mixed tool-call corpus with English replay. It costs continued-pretraining compute on top of SFT, erases the native tool-call format (every CPT checkpoint scores zero), and regresses English MMLU from 60.8 to 52.5. After adoption it can fail by almost never declining when no tool fits (6.9% correct), weak multi-turn calling, and calls that require verification before execution.
rationale: The recipe fits a single 24 GB GPU and delivers a large Tajik tool-calling gain, but the severe over-calling failure mode, CPT-induced skill loss, and English regression mean a team must validate abstention behavior and output checks on its own workload before production use.
technique: LoRA CPT + SFT for Tajik tool calling

claims.statement: The method replaces reliance on the base model's native tool-calling ability for Tajik with a two-stage recipe: LoRA continued pretraining on 1.49M Tajik documents followed by SFT on a mixed tool-call corpus with English replay. It costs continued-pretraining compute on top of SFT, erases the native tool-call format (every CPT checkpoint scores zero), and regresses English MMLU from 60.8 to 52.5. After adoption it can fail by almost never declining when no tool fits (6.9% correct), weak multi-turn calling, and calls that require verification before execution.
Strict tool-calling accuracy on Tajik prompts rises from 20.69 to 64.14 (+43.45 points, 95% CI +35.2 to +51.7); Tajik knowledge benchmark from 28.0 to 35.0.
